_comment: Mechanical encoding of products/around-the-world-80-days/day-01-london/scenes/README.md, section 'Linear cut', into render hints.
script: ordered tokens — s:N / s:N-M = narration sentence(s) by index (0-based, splitter in render_linear.mjs; the numbered list is in linear/render-log.md),
quiz:correct = correct option text + its feedback, chat:N = chip N question + answer (answer in voice2), overlay:N = the overlay text, game:list = the correct drag options.
No words are invented here: every token points at text that already exists in the scene JSON. Where the README seconds are shorter than the TTS,
render_linear.mjs end-cuts at a sentence boundary and logs it — the Narrator owns the final trim.
visuals: kind image|clip|player|scenecard|pending|quiz|chat|checklist|streetview; dur in seconds or omitted = share the remainder.
overlays: indices into scene.overlays, or {i, at, until} to re-time for the shorter linear scene. beds: {media, at, until}.

A4 2026-08-19: all sentence tokens re-derived after the A3n newcomer rewrite (old indices were stale and cut payoffs: Sheridan reveal, the route legs, the carpet-bag beat, the forgotten gas, the recipe). Linear cut is now ~13 min, longer than the original 11:42 plan, deliberately: coherence beats the target length.

A5 2026-08-19 (Narrator): the A4 tokens were derived from the STANDARD track but the film renders the CLEAR one (`--track clear`), whose sentences split differently (192 vs 181) — that mismatch is what produced the dangling references in review/fact-check-a5.md §4. Every `s:N` below is now re-derived against `narration.variants.clear` (`node render_linear.mjs <tour.json> --plan --track clear`) on three rules: keep the narrative spine; never leave a reference without its antecedent (Henry Poole is named before 'The firm says…', the club before 'It is real…', the carpet-bag before the packing list, the recipe card before it is mentioned); drop interactive-only instructions ('Tap any line', 'Drag in what goes', 'Save the card.', 'Now tap the longest leg', 'Ask him something', 'Take your time'). Re-derive after ANY script edit: the indices are per-track and per-wording.

A8 2026-08-19 (Content Preparer, queue item A6w): the linear cut no longer uses clip cards. A new visual kind `footage` points at a local, licence-clean file under <chapter>/media/files/ (h264 1280x720 25 fps, already normalised) — {kind:'footage', media:'M-xx', in_s?, dur?}. The scene JSONs record BOTH sources for the same shot: the YouTube entry keeps `use: "player"` (legal to embed, not to copy — review/rights-a6.md §1.2) and the local file carries `use: "linear"`. Scenes 02, 05, 13 and 18 changed here; 06 was already card-free. Scene 05 was RE-CUT 76 -> 42 s: no free source carries 76 s of continuous Pall Mall facade, so the beat is now a hyperlapse plus three facade stills (manifest-a6.md, rights-a6.md §3.6). Nothing in media/files/ is committed (.gitignore) — media/manifest.md carries the URL and the ffmpeg recipe for every file.

D6 2026-08-19 (Scene Developer, founder's instruction): Street View is a stop-and-look device, never transport (DECISIONS.md D6). Scene 04 count-the-steps stopped being a Street View walk and became a transport scene: the counting plays over the 1872 plan (M-30), then the street plays plainly as the cached open imagery (`panowalk` stops 5 and 6). Scene 05 pall-mall-pass is RETIRED and its entry deleted here — it existed only as the linear stand-in for the walk, and 04 now carries the same words in both cuts. Scene 15 look-up-the-cross joins the film as a slow pan over its own stop (`panowalk` stop 0, 44 m of 2025 Mapillary frames at walking pace): a film cannot offer a task, so the guide names what the player-traveller would have found. All s:N tokens for 04 and 15 are derived against the CLEAR track (`node render_linear.mjs <tour.json> --plan --track clear`).

count-the-steps._readme: D6 transport scene: the counting over the 1872 plan (M-30), then the street playing plainly — open-imagery walk, stop 5 (turn east into Pall Mall) and stop 6 (up to the Reform door, where the walk stops and looks), then the two neighbour façades; whole script — 97 s

visuals._why: BEAT A, the counting: the step numbers and the turns belong on the map, not on a street the traveller has to steer (D6). Different beat from scene 12's use of the same plate — see the scene's media note (crop + five stop-start strokes + step numbers); until the M-30a crop exists both scenes share the plate under a Ken Burns and the captions carry the difference.
BEAT B part 1: St James's Street × Pall Mall, the turn east into clubland (Mapillary 360°, 2024, 107 m). Falls back to the M-67 KartaView hyperlapse when media/files/panos/ is absent.

BEAT B part 2: the last 158 m up to the Reform door (Mapillary 360°, 2024-04). The scene's single stop-6 camera cue stops the walk in front of 104 Pall Mall at ≈ 64 s of the rendered scene and holds there while the guide names it. Falls back to the M-104 façade still (A11 2026-09-03: was M-20, a Brexit-demonstration photograph — see media/manifest.md §A11).

'A little to the left, No. 106, the Travellers…' — over its own façade. Swinging the open-imagery camera back onto it instead made the walk reverse 36 m. A11 2026-09-03: media M-69b -> M-106. The geograph file titled 'Travellers Club, Pall Mall' shows the REFORM Club (the 'CARLTON GARDENS SW1' sign is on its corner), so this eight-second shot named No. 106 over a picture of No. 104.

'And beyond it, No. 107, the Athenaeum. One turn of the head covers all three.' — the third façade closes the scene, so 06 can open on M-105 (the doorway itself, close) without repeating a frame across the seam.

count-the-steps._d6_note: Rendered length ≈ 90.2 s (clear track), so the five fixed visuals (46 + 14 + 20 + 8 + 9 = 97) scale to ≈ 42.8 / 13.0 / 18.6 / 7.4 / 8.4 s: the map holds the whole counting beat and hands over one second into 'And this is the street he is walking into'; the walk turns east at ≈ 43.5 s, stops in front of the Reform at ≈ 64 s, and the two neighbour façades take the last two lines. Overlay 0 is the step sticker and overlay 3 the clubland gloss — the renderer burns only pin/caption/lower-third, so neither is timed here. The six timed rows are in RENDERED seconds, each on the picture its words belong to.

(2) The `visuals` array was removed: it still asked for **M-69c**, which the rebuild deleted from the scene, so that 14-second segment was being silently dropped (same class of bug as A8's M-28), and it named none of the four interior pictures the scene has carried since 27 August. With no `visuals` hint the v0.9 renderer builds a photo scene from the scene's own slots, so the film now shows what the player shows. (3) Overlay times are the scene's windows scaled by the rendered length (~47 s / 70 s), because the renderer scales the photo slots the same way and these are picture captions.

charing-cross._a8_note: A8 (2026-08-19): clip card M-08 gone. The Eleanor Cross pin moved to 40-52 s so it sits over M-74 (the cross photographed from the station yard, c.1903) rather than over Trafalgar Square. Overlay 3 is a gloss and is not timed.
charing-cross._a11_note: A11 2026-09-03 (Narrator): scene lengthened 60 -> 75 s in BOTH cuts to fix the chapter's worst density (EN clear 2.35 w/s / 94 % fill -> 1.93 / 77 %); narration_at_s 2 matches the scene's new narration.starts_at_s, so the film opens on two seconds of Trafalgar Square before the guide speaks. NO sentence token was added or removed here and none was needed: this scene has no `script` key, so render_linear.mjs synthesises `s:0..s:N-1` from the current clear track (now 15 sentences, was 16) and speaks the whole thing. Every other scene's tokens index its own script and are untouched. Visuals re-cut 16/8/18/14/rest -> 16/8/16/12/23 = 75 s exactly (the renderer scales them to the rendered length, so these are also proportions): M-84 0-16 under the arrival, M-81 16-24 under the two 1865 dates, M-78 24-40 under the Embankment / clock tower / 'younger than his valet', M-74 40-52 arriving on 'One thing you cannot see', M-51 52-75 arriving on 'A barefoot woman with a child asks for money.' (~51 s) and holding through the last three sentences and ~11 s of silence — the scene's designed rest (positioning.md: silence is content). The last 35 s are now IDENTICAL to the player's, which uses the same M-74 40-52 / M-51 52-75. Overlays: [0] untimed, so it keeps the scene's own 10-24 s; the Eleanor Cross pin moves 42-54 -> 41-51 to stay over M-74 (A8's rule); the twenty-guineas caption moves 56-66 -> 61-72 to land after its sentence, over M-51. Overlay 3 is a gloss and is not burned.
